profile.reading:
Csquare IAD2-A sits at 22810 International Drive, Sterling, Virginia 20166, part of Csquare's IAD2 campus in Loudoun County, described by Csquare's own materials as "two additional pods" connected by dark fiber to the nearby IAD1 campus. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists this building individually as "IAD2_A," 49,427 square feet sellable, 55.7 percent leased and Csquare-owned as of March 31, 2026; Csquare's public spec sheet gives a campus-wide total of 48,169 square feet raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, notably without the ENERGY STAR rating Csquare cites for its IAD1 campus. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD2 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026. The dark-fiber link Csquare describes between IAD2 and the nearby IAD1 campus allows customers at either site to interconnect directly without routing traffic through a third-party carrier hotel, a common colocation-industry practice for operators with multiple nearby buildings in the same metro.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

profile.research_note: Sqft is the SEC S-1 per-building sellable figure for IAD2-A (49,427 sqft); Csquare's public spec sheet gives only a campus-wide raised-floor total (48,169 sqft) covering both IAD2-A and IAD2-B, not broken out, so that figure was not used. Power figures (35.8MW utility, 8.5MW UPS, 20MW generator) are campus-wide only, so no capacity figure was attributed. IAD2 notably lacks the ENERGY STAR rating Csquare cites for IAD1.

reading.body:
IAD2-A is one of two adjacent buildings on Csquare's Sterling campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, part of a 48,169 square foot raised floor facility with 35.8 megawatts of utility power published as a combined campus figure. The campus holds SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it to host regulated workloads and enterprise infrastructure. Csquare interconnects IAD2 to its nearby IAD1 campus via dark fiber, allowing customers to move traffic between sites without routing through external carriers.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the 35.8 megawatt campus utility power suggests roughly 900 racks of capacity, though the published figure does not distinguish between IT load and facility overhead. The facility's raised floor and power density are consistent with colocation and enterprise hosting rather than the densest hyperscale AI configurations, which commonly exceed 100 kilowatts per rack when averaged across an entire campus.

Virginia ranks 24th nationally among facilities with published power capacity, with 1,375 megawatts across 23 mapped sites. Csquare's disclosed portfolio of 389 megawatts across 64 facilities makes it a material operator in the broader hyperscale market, though this single campus does not rank among Virginia's largest published facilities and sits in a region where published capacity is concentrated among a small number of operators.
